subject: Performance guardrails & p95/concurrency recap — Neurolytics
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ethan Walsh <ethan.walsh@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance guardrails & p95/concurrency recap — Neurolytics

Ethan — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so your team can confirm and so we can line up the right next steps. I tried to keep this tight; call out anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Bursty ingestion from batch analytics jobs causes momentary concurrency spikes (up to ~2.5x baseline) that lead to token queuing and tail latency.
- Streaming UX suffers when users expect sub-200ms generation for short responses (chat-like flows).
- Current cache hits are low for LLM prefix reuse (client-side caching is limited).

Current stack notes you shared:
- Frontend: React app + websocket streaming for UX.
- Serving: In-house Triton-based endpoints behind HAProxy; autoscaling on node count, not on request-level batching.
- Observability: Prometheus + custom traces, but limited token-level cost breakdown.

Success criteria (what you told us):
- p95 end-to-end token latency for streaming interactions <= 120ms for 1–2 token responses during steady state.
- Support 2k concurrent active sessions with 3k QPS burst capacity without >5% request queuing.
- No functional regression in output quality (same prompts, same model topology).

Immediate risks we identified:
- Triton deployment pattern doesn't surface per-request batching/priority, so latency-sensitive streaming may get batched into high-latency buckets.
- Cold start/triton container spin-up during bursts causing p95 spikes.

Proposed guardrails and measures (what Redwood can do):
1) Streaming-priority routing: separate low-latency streaming pool for short-response chat (smaller batch sizes, reserved capacity).
2) KV/prefix caching layer: automatic prefix cache to reduce recomputation for conversational turns.
3) Batching policy recommendations: dynamic batching thresholds based on sequence length distribution + token-budgeted preemption.
4) Trial: 2-week dedicated capacity trial (small pool sized for 2k concurrency) with token-level telemetry and a playbook to validate p95 targets.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- Neurolytics to confirm p95 target (I have 150ms noted; please confirm if 120ms is the true goal) — Ethan (reply) — by EOD Wed 6/16.
- Redwood to provide one-pager with proposed capacity profile and expected cost delta for the 2-week trial — Irene — by Thu 6/17. (attached: performance_guardrails_onepager.pdf)
- Technical deep-dive (Triton + autoscaling knobs) with Neurolytics SREs — propose Fri 6/18 10:00 PT — Vivek to lead.

Questions for you (so we prep correctly):
1) What percentage of interactions are single-token responses vs. multi-token (>8 tokens)? Any distribution samples you can share help tune batching policy.
2) Are there any regulatory/traffic egress constraints (EU-only, HIPAA) we should consider for the trial?

Thanks again — if that all looks right I’ll spin up the trial plan and calendar the deep dive.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0193
Redwood Inference

Attachment: performance_guardrails_onepager.pdf (1 page, PDF)
From: Ethan Walsh <ethan.walsh@neurolytics.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance guardrails & p95/concurrency recap — Neurolytics

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Our internal target is actually 120ms p95 for the short streaming interactions (I should have been clearer on the call).
- The burst behavior: baseline concurrency is ~800 active sessions; spikes up to ~2,000–2,500 are typically 3–7 minutes and align with ETL batch windows.
- I attached a small sample of latency traces/output counts (neurolytics_latency_samples.csv) that shows the distribution we see during spikes.

On regulatory: not HIPAA, but EU customers are routed through a regional gateway; trial should be in US-only region to start.

We’re good with the proposed deep dive on 6/18 10:00 PT — have Matt (SRE lead) and Priya (backend PM) join as well.

Ethan Walsh
Head of Product, Neurolytics
ethan.walsh@neurolytics.ai
(650) 555-2234

Attachment: neurolytics_latency_samples.csv (CSV, ~2.1MB)

Subject: Re: Performance guardrails & p95/concurrency recap — Neurolytics

Perfect — thanks for confirming the 120ms p95 target and the US-only trial constraint. I’ll update the one-pager with expected sizing for a 2k concurrent reserved pool that aims to meet the 120ms p95 for short flows.

Actions I’ll take now:
- Send updated one-pager (sizing + cost estimate) tomorrow morning 6/15.
- Share calendar invite for technical deep dive 6/18 10:00 PT and include a short agenda (Triton topology, batching/priorities, telemetry hooks).
- Prepare a short checklist for Neurolytics SRE to collect (token distribution sample, current autoscaler config, model sharding info).

If you can drop the sample token distribution ahead of the call that will speed tuning — thanks.

Talk soon,
Irene
